transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

I’m convinced certain people in my professional and art circles are secretly working together to damage my reputation and my practice, even though everyone keeps telling me it’s not really happening. It’s just become incredibly stressful to deal with, and my sister insisted I come talk to someone because I can't shake this feeling.

Besides feeling that people are plotting against you, have you been hearing or seeing things that others don’t, or have others said your speech or behavior has become confused or disorganized? If so, when did this start?

No, I haven't experienced hearing or seeing things that others don't, and no one has told me that my speech or behavior seems confused or disorganized. It's really just this constant, stressful feeling that people are actively coordinating against me.
How long have you been convinced that these people are working together against you? Did it come on suddenly over days to weeks, or has it been present for months or longer?

The general worries and pulling away started gradually about two years ago after a bad breakup. However, this really intense, specific conviction that people are actively coordinating to ruin my reputation has been constant and nonstop for the last couple of months.

Outside of this belief that people are plotting against you, have you had a noticeable decline in work, self-care, motivation, or emotional expression over the past couple of years? For example, have you become much less interested in people or activities, or has it been hard to keep up with daily responsibilities?

Yes, my motivation has completely plummeted over the last couple of years; I mostly just sit in my apartment with the TV on mute, ignoring texts and lacking the energy to cook or go out. When I do force myself to leave, I feel totally flat and disconnected, and my financial practice has really suffered because I've cut my hours and lost several long-term clients.

Before the belief about people plotting against you became intense, were you already spending a lot of time withdrawn, emotionally flat, and neglecting work or self-care? Or did those problems mainly start because of the belief itself?

The withdrawal, emotional flatness, and neglect of my practice actually started gradually in the months after my breakup over two years ago and have slowly worsened since then. The intense belief that people are actively coordinating to ruin my reputation is much more recent, only becoming constant over the last couple of months.

Based on this conversation, F22.0 now seems less likely because the patient describes a gradual 2-year history of prominent withdrawal, reduced motivation, flat/disconnected affect, neglect of self-care, and occupational decline that clearly preceded the fixed persecutory belief. That broader deterioration is more consistent with a schizophrenia-spectrum disorder than an isolated persistent delusional disorder, especially since there are no hallucinations or disorganization but there are significant negative-type symptoms and functional decline. Therefore the current candidate list is narrowed to [F20.0].

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has a persistent persecutory delusion with a prodromal/residual course marked by over two years of negative symptoms and functional decline that clearly preceded the recent intensification of psychotic symptoms. There are no hallucinations or disorganization, but schizophrenia can be diagnosed when delusions are present along with prominent negative symptoms, deterioration in functioning, and an overall duration exceeding 6 months.
